speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You've presented with increasing pain and swelling in your left knee for two months; to begin my assessment, can you describe the specific location of the pain and whether it worsens with activity or rest?

speaker: Patient
text: 24-year-old male. The patient reports increasing pain and swelling of the left knee over 2 months. Describes the pain as severe enough to awaken him from sleep on several occasions. States he tried taking ibuprofen with no relief. No family or personal history of significant illnesses.

speaker: Doctor
text: That is concerning; please tell me, was there a specific injury or trauma to your knee before the pain began, or did it start spontaneously? Also, have you noticed any redness, warmth, or a visible limp?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe pain and swelling in the left knee. I also have Pain intensifying over 2 months, Painful awakenings during night, No relief with ibuprofen.

speaker: Doctor
text: No specific injury occurred, and I see no redness or warmth; given the night pain that wakes you and lack of relief with ibuprofen, this suggests an inflammatory or neoplastic process rather than simple arthritis. REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, CRP, and Serum Uric Acid. REQUEST IMAGES: Left Knee X-Ray (AP, Lateral, and Sunrise view).
